title: Implement shared subscription manager event fanout and immutable cache
description:
Implement MarketDataService in mike_trade/market_data/service.py and the shared market-data cache in mike_trade/market_data/cache.py, with unit tests in tests/unit/test_data_fanout.py.

MarketDataService:
- Owns exactly one streaming adapter, the Alpaca stream from g.1 or any adapter injected through the port, plus the REST fallback poller from g.2.
- Maintains a reference-counted subscription registry keyed by (symbol, channel). Every live, paper, and shadow scenario consumer registers interest. The union is subscribed once: the first consumer triggers the upstream subscribe and the last unregister triggers the upstream unsubscribe.
- Fans each normalized immutable event out to all registered consumers through bounded per-consumer queues. A slow consumer gets an explicit overflow/drop counter and degraded flag, and must not block other consumers or the ingest loop.
- Switches to REST polling fallback when the stream is disconnected, and back when it recovers, while preserving provenance (source='stream' vs 'rest_poll').
- Exposes read-only accessors only. Strategies receive context objects and never get a network handle.

cache.py:
- Stores the latest quote and latest trade per symbol, compact decision evidence, candle-builder inputs, completed candles in a bounded ring per symbol/timeframe, indicator rolling-state slots, and freshness metadata (provider_source_ts, receive_ts, feed_id).
- All stored values are immutable, frozen dataclasses or tuples. Readers get snapshots, never mutable internals.
- Every collection is bounded, so the cache cannot grow into a raw session tick archive.
- The cache refuses to merge events whose feed_id differs from the symbol's established feed unless the feed is explicitly reset.

Use asyncio with an injected clock. Tests use fake stream/poller adapters.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/market_data/alpaca_stream.py (g.1) for event types, the state observer, and subscription API
- mike_trade/market_data/alpaca_history.py and mike_trade/market_data/polling.py (g.2) for the fallback poller API and snapshot provenance
- mike_trade/ domain/ports, candle and indicator modules from earlier phases that consume cached data (if present)
acceptance_criteria: With N consumers (including at least two shadow scenarios and one paper consumer) registering the same (symbol, channel), the upstream adapter receives exactly one subscribe call; a test asserts the count.
The upstream unsubscribe happens only when the last consumer unregisters; a test verifies the reference counting.
Every registered consumer receives every event for its subscriptions, and the delivered event is the same immutable object or an equal frozen copy; mutating it raises an error, which a test verifies.
A blocked or slow consumer whose bounded queue fills records an overflow count and a degraded flag, while other consumers still receive events promptly; a test covers this.

When the fake stream reports DISCONNECTED, the service activates the polling fallback, cached updates carry source='rest_poll' provenance, and on reconnect it returns to source='stream'; a test covers this.
Cache collections enforce the configured maximum sizes (the completed-candle ring and evidence buffer), and older entries are evicted; a test verifies no unbounded growth over many events.
The cache rejects an event whose feed_id conflicts with the symbol's established feed_id; a negative test covers this.
Cache read accessors return immutable snapshots that carry provider_source_ts, receive_ts, and feed_id.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
expose network clients or broker handles to strategies
subscribe per strategy or per scenario
use network access or real credentials in tests
run broad test suites or backtests
